feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: in iteration 0 (baseline, 60 trials) every run went off track after about one line loss, with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m and low steering oscillation (0.11 to 0.15). In iteration 1, widening the sensors to ±0.045 m cut oval line losses from 1.05 to 0.55, so sensing reach is real. But s-bend and slalom still lost the line once per run (1.0), and oval progress fell from 0.175 to 0.121. In iteration 2 (mass 0.6 kg), s-bend and slalom still showed 1.0 line losses with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m, while oval losses fell to 0.35. Mass reduction alone did not clear those tracks, so turn authority is the remaining constraint there. I kept the controller gains and speed unchanged so the wheel_track change reads cleanly. Read the next race as follows: if s-bend and slalom line losses reach 0 with max_error below about 0.055 m, keep the geometry and check oval progress. If losses stay at 1 with max_error at the limit, the turn-authority lever is spent, so widen the sensors. If losses are gone but oval progress stays near 0.12, the shortfall is controller speed, which I will fix in the controller.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom still shows line_loss_events of 1 with max_error at or above 0.06 m after this race: keep mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m, and widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.054 with 0.027 m steps, keeping sensor_size 0.012 m. Iteration 1 showed ±0.045 m cut oval line losses from 1.05 to 0.55, and iteration 0 showed the array reaching only about ±0.036 m.

If line losses reach 0 on all development tracks but oval progress stays near 0.12: keep the geometry as proposed. The shortfall is controller speed, which I will address by raising base_speed, not by narrowing further.

If wheel_track 0.09 m makes oval progress fall below 0.12 without clearing the s-bend and slalom losses: return to wheel_track 0.10 m, the iteration 2 setting. Iteration 1 showed that progress fell when the track was first narrowed, so the track may be costing progress, not gaining turn authority.
